issues.legal_issue: A plaint cannot be rejected at the threshold for limitation when, read as a whole and treated as true, its allegations do not show that the suit is time-barred.
material_facts: The plaintiffs alleged that they learned of the relevant property transactions in 1999 and filed the suits in 2002.
The suits sought declarations of title and possession, along with related reliefs.
The defendants sought rejection of the plaints, relying in part on limitation.
issues.conclusion: The plaints did not disclose on their face that the suits were barred by limitation, so rejection under Order VII Rule 11 was not justified; the suits were to be decided on their merits.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, rejection of a plaint is a drastic threshold power subject to stringent conditions. The plaint must be read as a whole, and its averments must be accepted as true; the defendants’ written statement or assertions in their rejection application are immaterial at this stage. A plaint may be rejected only where it ex facie discloses no cause of action or shows that the suit is barred by law; otherwise, the claims must be adjudicated at trial. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

rule.if: civil_suit_plaint_rejection_application and plaint_read_as_whole and pleaded_discovery_within_three_years_before_filing and no_bar_apparent_on_plaint

predicates.civil_suit_plaint_rejection_application: A party in a civil suit applied to have the plaint rejected at the threshold.
predicates.plaint_read_as_whole: The court assessed the plaint as a whole and treated its factual allegations as true for the application.
predicates.pleaded_discovery_within_three_years_bef: The plaintiffs alleged that they discovered the essential facts within three years before filing the suit.
predicates.no_bar_apparent_on_plaint: The allegations in the plaint did not themselves show that the suit was barred by law.
predicates.plaint_not_rejected_at_threshold: The plaint is not rejected at the threshold and the claims proceed for adjudication.

issues.definition: When a civil plaint-rejection application is assessed on the whole plaint, the plaintiffs plead discovery within three years before filing, and no legal bar appears from the plaint, the plaint proceeds for adjudication rather than being rejected at the threshold.

issues.legal_issue: The prohibition on benami transactions does not bar a suit seeking a declaration of title and possession where the suit is not for recovery of property held benami by the defendants.
material_facts: The suits sought declarations of the plaintiffs’ title and recovery of possession from the defendants.
One suit also sought cancellation of instruments concerning the property.
The claims were not suits to recover property held benami by the defendants.
issues.conclusion: The Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Act did not bar the suits because they sought declarations of title and possession, rather than recovery of property held benami by the defendants.
issues.legal_principle: The Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Act, 1988 did not apply on the pleaded facts because the suits were not for recovery of property held benami by the defendants; they were for declarations of title and recovery of possession. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

predicates.civil_title_and_possession_suit: The proceeding is a civil suit concerning title to and possession of property.
predicates.seeks_declaration_of_title_and_possessio: The plaintiffs seek a declaration of title and recovery of possession from the defendants.
predicates.suit_seeks_recovery_of_property_held_ben: The suit seeks recovery of property alleged to be held benami by the defendants.
predicates.benami_bar_does_not_apply: The prohibition on benami transactions does not bar the suit.

issues.definition: A civil suit seeking a declaration of title and possession is not barred when it is not a suit to recover property held benami by the defendants.
